basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 18.' and it opens 'Vers. 18. Juxta convallem Mambre. Quod est in Hebron. Hebron civitas est in tribu Juda,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 18. Juxta convallem Mambre. Quod est in Hebron. Hebron civitas est in tribu Juda, quae alio nomine Cariatharbe dicitur, id est civitas quatuor. Cariath enim Hebraice civitas, arbe, quatuor. Ibi enim | situs est Adam maximus, et Abraham, et Isaac et Jacob. Convallis Mambre ab uno amicorum Abraham dicta est qui Mambre vocabatur.
